tool.name: FAIRe2QIIME
tool.description: make QIIME 2 sample metadata and manifests from a FAIRe workbook
tool.command: set -o pipefail; ln -s '$input_file' input.xlsx && python '$__tool_directory__/normalise_faire.py' input.xlsx normalised.xlsx --check_column '$sample_name_column' #if $suffix.use_suffix == 'yes': --check_column '$suffix.column_suffix' #end if #if $manifests.write_manifests == 'yes': --check_filled filename #end if > log.txt && mkdir out && ## FAIRe2QIIME names files by gene and fragment; assays that share them are converted one at a time python '$__tool_directory__/faire2qiime_by_assay.py' '$__tool_directory__/faire2qiime.py' normalised.xlsx out -- --sample_name_column '$sample_name_column' #if $manifests.write_manifests == 'yes': --absolute_path_sequences '$manifests.absolute_path_sequences' #else: --absolute_path_sequences /not/used #end if #if $suffix.use_suffix == 'yes': --column_suffix '$suffix.column_suffix' --direction_suffix '$suffix.direction_suffix' --num_chars_suffix $suffix.num_chars_suffix --delimiter_suffix '$suffix.delimiter_suffix' #end if | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -v -e 'pyfiglet' -e '^=*$' -e '^ *$' >> log.txt && ## A check that no file was written twice (faire2qiime_by_assay.py should prevent it). dup=\$(grep -o 'Generated [a-z]* file .*' log.txt | sort | uniq -d || true) && if [ -n "\$dup" ]; then echo "ERROR: two or more assays share the same target_gene and target_subfragment, so FAIRe2QIIME wrote these files more than once and kept only the last assay: \$dup. Give each assay its own target_subfragment in projectMetadata, or run the tool on a workbook with one of the assays." >&2; exit 1; fi && cp log.txt '$log'

param.name: input_file
param.label: FAIRe metadata workbook
param.help: Excel workbook with projectMetadata, sampleMetadata and experimentRunMetadata sheets. Both the FAIRe layout (assay1, assay2 ... columns, as made by FAIRe-ator) and the FAIRe-NOAA layout are accepted.

param.name: sample_name_column
param.label: Column to use as the QIIME 2 sample ID
param.help: Copied to a first column called sample_name. It must match the sample IDs you use when importing reads into QIIME 2. lib_id is usually the right choice because it is unique per library.

param.name: write_manifests
param.label: Write QIIME 2 manifest files?
param.help: Manifests list the forward and reverse fastq file of each sample, one file per sequencing run and assay.

param.name: absolute_path_sequences
param.label: Folder that holds the sequencing run folders
param.help: The manifests give each file as FOLDER/seq_run_id/filename. Enter the folder on the computer where you will run QIIME 2 (for example your HPC project folder). Galaxy cannot see these files; the path is only written into the manifests.

validator.message: Enter an absolute path starting with /

param.name: use_suffix
param.label: Make repeated samp_name values unique?
param.help: Adds a samp_name_unique column. Samples that appear more than once within an assay (for example resequenced in a second run) get a suffix taken from another column.

param.name: column_suffix
param.label: Column to take the suffix from

param.name: delimiter_suffix
param.label: Text to put before the suffix

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool reads a FAIRe metadata workbook and writes the files that QIIME 2 needs to start an amplicon analysis:
- one **sample metadata** file for each assay, which joins experimentRunMetadata, sampleMetadata, and the project-level and assay-level values from projectMetadata; - if you ask for them, one **manifest** for each sequencing run and assay, which lists the forward and reverse fastq file for each sample.
The files are named from the project_id, the target gene and subfragment, and the seq_run_id, for example *myproject_COI-Leray_metadata* and *RUN01_COI-Leray_manifest*. If two assays have the same target gene and subfragment (for example three 12S assays), each assay is converted on its own and every file is named by its assay_name, for example *myproject_MiFish-U_metadata*.
-----
**Inputs**
The tool takes a FAIRe workbook (.xlsx) with projectMetadata, sampleMetadata and experimentRunMetadata sheets. projectMetadata needs target_gene, and ideally target_subfragment, for each assay.
FAIRe2QIIME was written for the FAIRe-NOAA layout, where each assay has a projectMetadata column named after it. Workbooks from FAIRe-ator use columns called assay1, assay2 ... (or project_level for a single assay). This tool relabels those columns by their assay_name before conversion, so both layouts work, and the log records what was relabelled.
Values reach the QIIME 2 files as they are written in the workbook. On its own, FAIRe2QIIME treats a # anywhere in a cell as the start of a comment, so *Sta1 #2* becomes *Sta1* and the rest of that sample's row is lost, and it reads a column of IDs such as 001, 002 as numbers (1, 2). While FAIRe2QIIME runs, this tool reads the workbook for it in a way that avoids both.
-----
**Outputs**
- **QIIME 2 metadata** (a collection of tabular files). The first column, sample_name, holds the values of the column you chose as the sample ID. Columns that are empty for every sample are dropped, and repeated column names get a _SAMPLE or _PROJECT suffix. - **QIIME 2 manifests** (a collection, if you ask for them). Each file has the columns sample-id, forward-absolute-filepath and reverse-absolute-filepath, which is the *PairedEndFastqManifestPhred33V2* format for **qiime tools import**. - **log**: a record of the run.
**About the manifests**
The manifests point to files on the computer where you will run QIIME 2, and Galaxy does not check that the files exist. If you are importing reads into QIIME 2 *within Galaxy*, you do not need the manifests. Instead, build a paired collection of your fastq files, with element identifiers that match the sample_name column, and use the metadata file from this tool.
@HELP_FAIRE_GUIDE@
-----
**Credits**
This tool runs `FAIRe2QIIME <https://github.com/aomlomics/faire2qiime>`_ (CC0) from NOAA 'Omics, after a small Galaxy step that relabels FAIRe assay columns and checks the chosen columns exist. The FAIRe checklist is described in Takahashi et al. (2025) *Environmental DNA* 7: e70100. The Galaxy tool was written by Oliver Berry (CSIRO), with Claude (Anthropic).
